content: A problem-oriented medical record is a structured system of documentation in which a comprehensive list of a patient’s medical problems is created. For each identified problem, all relevant information—including the patient’s medical history, physical examination findings, laboratory results, and other pertinent data—is organized and recorded under the corresponding problem heading. This approach to medical record-keeping was first introduced in 1968 by Dr. Larry Weed. The responsibility for maintaining accurate and up-to-date problem lists has been proposed to lie with healthcare providers. However, it is important to note that problem lists are not always complete. Incomplete problem lists can negatively impact the quality of medical care provided and may pose risks to patient safety.
